activation.details: Profiles persist after the one-time creation; aliases apply to each new shell; no reboot needed.

payload.effects: Two access points on isolated subnets NATed through the wired uplink; clients get fast DHCP and DNS from per-connection dnsmasq; switching modes briefly restarts the involved radios and clients re-associate; nothing runs as an added daemon beyond NetworkManager's own ephemeral dnsmasq.
payload.explanation: Install path is three steps: one-time profile creation (sudo, the shared passphrase is prompted with read -s and only ever lands in root-owned NetworkManager connection files, never in the repo), alias installation into ~/.alias, and optional dnsmasq-shared drop-ins. Machine-specific values live in a gitignored config.sh sourced through one shared loader: SSID prefix, the two radio interface names, subnet gateways, base and wide regulatory country codes, optional resolver address; published scripts therefore keep no personal values. Mode scripts always begin from the full-off baseline and end asserting the intended regulatory country, so switching is idempotent, and web-off restores the base country.

steps: git clone the repository into ~/web-tools, copy config.example.sh to config.sh, set SSID_PREFIX, the radio interface names from iw dev, the two subnet gateway hosts, and the base and wide regulatory country codes
Run ./install.sh to add the web-* aliases to ~/.alias idempotently, then reload the shell
Create the profiles once: sudo ./setup-profiles.sh (it prompts for the shared passphrase interactively)
Optional: copy the two files under etc/NetworkManager/dnsmasq-shared.d/ into that system directory for DHCP/DNS tuning and a local resolver for clients

Operate with the aliases: web-dual or web-two for normal use, web-max variants for the 160 MHz access point, web-off to stop everything and restore the base regulatory country, web-status for the read-only live view

payload.rollback: sudo nmcli connection delete on each WEB-* profile, remove the alias block from the shell alias file, remove the two optional dnsmasq drop-ins; no service is installed by the suite itself.
payload.validation_plan: web-status shows both access points with the expected channels and widths and the intended regulatory country; a test client joins each SSID, receives an address in the configured range, and name resolution goes through the advertised resolver.
